we can use the fuzzy predicates in the same way as crisp predicates in a query language, and that we can use them to query fuzzy regions in the same way we can query crisp regions.
we have defined a model for representing fuzzy regions, we have defined topological predicates for fuzzy regions and we have shown that these predicates can be used in a query language.
we present a model of fuzzy topological predicates, we show some properties of them, and we integrate the predicates into a query language for spatial databases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to extend spatial query languages with predicates that are able to express topological relationships between regions with indeterminate boundaries.
the question of how topological relationships between fuzzy regions can be modeled and used in spatial data handling and spatial reasoning.
the question: how to define, characterize, and integrate topological predicates for fuzzy regions into query languages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the integration of the proposed model into spatial data handling and spatial reasoning is a promising approach.
the integration of topological predicates into query languages for handling spatial data with fuzzy boundaries is feasible and that the predicates have a wide range of applications.
the integration of fuzzy predicates into a query language can be done without any major problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fuzzy predicates between fuzzy regions are defined and their properties are shown.
we have developed a fuzzy model for spatial objects with vague or imprecise boundaries and that we have integrated it into a query language for spatial databases.

the integration of fuzzy topological predicates into spatial query languages provides an important tool to model and handle spatial phenomena and their relationships in a more adequate and more realistic way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fuzzy topological predicates can be used as a basis for a fuzzy query language that can handle topological relationships between fuzzy regions.
the proposed model and predicates provide a solid foundation for a fuzzy extension of the well-known topological query language Region Connection Calculus.
fuzzy predicates can serve as an extension to the existing crisp topological predicates in spatial database systems.
